runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets surged overnight, led by Japan's Nikkei 225 climbing ~1.2% to 39,240 after Nvidia's blockbuster Q2 earnings and bullish FY2028 guidance from CFO Colette Kress sent semiconductor-related names sharply higher. South Korean KOSPI gained on Hynix and Samsung strength; Chinese markets were mixed as lingering property-sector concerns offset the global tech tailwind. The yen weakened modestly against the dollar, providing additional export-sector support for Japanese equities.

European markets opened mixed on Thursday morning. Germany's DAX dipped ~0.3% near 19,920 after Wednesday's US PCE inflation data — headline 3.7% YoY and core 3.3% YoY, both above consensus — reignited rate-hike fears and pushed the 10-year yield to 4.58%. The FTSE 100 modestly outperformed at +0.4% near 8,485, supported by commodity-linked names and resilient UK consumer data. The ECB remains in watch mode as European inflation stays sticky, and Boston Fed President Collins reinforced the hawkish stance overnight, warning rates must rise unless a sustained drop in inflation materializes.

US equity futures are pointing to a positive open as Nvidia's after-hours surge carries forward. S&P 500 futures are +0.35%, Nasdaq 100 futures +0.66%, Dow futures +0.25% — with prediction markets pricing a 71% probability of a higher open. Key macro catalysts today include weekly initial jobless claims (consensus 407,000), ISM Manufacturing at 10am (consensus 48.5, contractionary), and a heavy earnings slate: Dollar Tree (DLTR), Dollar General (DG), Marvell Technology (MRVL), Workday (WDAY), Best Buy (BBY), Autodesk (ADSK), Affirm (AFRM), and Ulta Beauty (ULTA). S&P 500 Q2 earnings growth is now tracking +50% YoY — an extraordinary figure driven largely by AI infrastructure investment. VIX sits at 14.8, reflecting relative calm despite the macro uncertainty.

ideas.catalyst: CFO Colette Kress guided to strong FY2028 revenue growth on Wednesday's Q2 earnings call, easing fears of an AI capex slowdown.
ideas.thesis: Nvidia remains the dominant supplier of GPUs for AI training and inference, with demand from hyperscalers and sovereign AI programs sustaining backlog well into FY2028. The bullish multi-year revenue guide validates that enterprise AI buildout is accelerating, not plateauing.
ideas.key_risk: Export control escalation targeting advanced GPU shipments to China or policy-driven capex cuts from hyperscalers.

ideas.catalyst: FDA PDUFA decision today on once-daily single-tablet HIV regimen combining bictegravir and lenacapavir — a potentially transformative all-in-one pill for virologically-suppressed patients.
ideas.thesis: Gilead's HIV franchise grew 12% YoY to $5.7B in Q2, and an FDA approval of the bictegravir/lenacapavir combination would extend its dominant HIV market position with a best-in-class convenience profile. EU already approved Trodelvy in the same period, demonstrating regulatory momentum across its pipeline.
ideas.key_risk: FDA issues a complete response letter requesting additional clinical data, triggering a sharp pullback given elevated positioning.

ideas.catalyst: Marvell reports Q2 FY27 earnings today after market close; consensus expects strong custom AI ASIC revenue from Amazon and Google partnerships.
ideas.thesis: Marvell has emerged as the leading custom ASIC designer for hyperscaler AI chips, with its AWS Trainium and Google TPU partnerships driving a multi-year revenue ramp that should be further validated in today's Q2 report. Data center revenue growth has been tracking well above consensus estimates.
ideas.key_risk: Guidance disappoints on hyperscaler ASIC timeline delays or consumer/enterprise networking weakness offsets data center strength.

ideas.catalyst: BMO Capital upgraded FSLR to Outperform from Market Perform today with a $265 price target, citing underappreciated domestic manufacturing capacity advantages under IRA provisions.
ideas.thesis: First Solar is the only US-headquartered large-scale solar panel manufacturer, giving it a structural edge under the Inflation Reduction Act's manufacturing tax credits that foreign competitors cannot replicate. The BMO upgrade and $265 target imply significant upside from current levels as utility-scale solar demand accelerates.
ideas.key_risk: IRA subsidy rollback risk from Congressional action or regulatory reinterpretation that eliminates the domestic manufacturing premium.

sources.label: Thursday Analyst Calls — The Globe and Mail

ideas.catalyst: CrowdStrike surged on Q2 earnings that beat consensus, with AI-powered Falcon platform driving net-new ARR growth above expectations as enterprises consolidate security vendors.
ideas.thesis: CrowdStrike's Falcon platform is benefiting from dual tailwinds: the shift to AI-native threat detection and the enterprise preference to consolidate security spending onto fewer, more capable platforms. Q2 results confirmed ARR growth reacceleration, suggesting the recovery from last year's operational disruption is complete.
ideas.key_risk: Another major platform outage or a competitor offering comparable AI capabilities at a meaningfully lower price point.

sources.label: Earnings Live Updates Q2 — Yahoo Finance

ideas.catalyst: Baird upgraded SNPS to Outperform today with a $560 price target, citing record chip design activity driven by AI accelerator proliferation and custom silicon from hyperscalers.
ideas.thesis: Synopsys is the duopoly leader in electronic design automation software, which every chip design — from Nvidia GPUs to custom hyperscaler ASICs — must run through. The explosion in AI chip design creates a multi-year EDA spending cycle that is highly recurring and difficult to displace.
ideas.key_risk: Proposed Ansys merger regulatory complications or an economic downturn reducing semiconductor R&D budgets.

ideas.catalyst: Dollar Tree reports Q2 FY26 earnings before the open today; hot PCE (3.7% headline) compresses the value proposition while tariff-related cost headwinds weigh on margins.
ideas.thesis: Dollar Tree's core customer base faces a squeeze from persistent inflation that erodes purchasing power faster than the retailer can pass through price increases on its fixed-price model. Tariff-related COGS inflation and integration costs from Family Dollar remain a structural drag on EBIT margins.
ideas.key_risk: A beat-and-raise quarter driven by trade-down from higher-income consumers seeking value, triggering a sharp short squeeze.

ideas.catalyst: Bank of America upgraded OKTA to Neutral from Underperform with a $170 target today, following Q2 earnings that showed reaccelerating net-new customer growth and improved profitability.
ideas.thesis: Okta's recovery from its 2023 data breach crisis has progressed further than the prior BofA Underperform rating implied, with customer attrition stabilizing and the AI-assisted identity governance platform gaining traction in enterprise deals. The upgrade from a notable bear removes a key overhang.
ideas.key_risk: Another security incident or customer churn resurgence that reignites concerns about the platform's trustworthiness.

ideas.catalyst: Dollar General reports Q2 FY26 today; core low-income customer base is most exposed to 3.7% headline PCE inflation and tightening credit, with rising shrink and labor costs adding additional margin pressure.
ideas.thesis: Dollar General serves the most economically stressed consumer cohort in US retail; with PCE running hot and unemployment creeping higher, its core shopper is cutting discretionary purchases and defaulting on store credit, pressuring comp sales and gross margins simultaneously. Same-store sales momentum has been decelerating for three consecutive quarters.
ideas.key_risk: A surprise beat on core consumables strength shows the low-income consumer is more resilient than feared, triggering a relief rally.

ideas.catalyst: Workday reports Q2 FY27 earnings today; AI-enhanced HCM and financial planning modules are driving deal expansion and net revenue retention improvements among large enterprise clients.
ideas.thesis: Workday is embedding AI across its human capital management and financial planning suites, enabling upsell to existing customers and accelerating competitive displacement of legacy SAP and Oracle HR systems. Q2 results should demonstrate improving subscription revenue growth and margin expansion as the AI monetization cycle gains traction.
ideas.key_risk: Macro-driven enterprise software spending freeze forces CFOs to delay Workday expansion projects, suppressing net revenue retention.

deals.headline: Gilead Sciences FDA PDUFA Decision: Once-Daily HIV Regimen
deals.description: The FDA is expected to issue a decision today on Gilead's once-daily single-tablet HIV regimen combining bictegravir and lenacapavir for virologically-suppressed patients. Gilead's HIV franchise generated $5.7B in Q2 revenue (+12% YoY), and approval would extend its dominant HIV market leadership with an unprecedented convenience profile.
deals.impact: High — binary event, potential 10-20% move in GILD

deals.headline: Nvidia Q2 Beat + Bullish FY2028 Revenue Guidance
deals.description: Nvidia reported Q2 earnings Wednesday after-hours that significantly beat consensus, with CFO Colette Kress signaling strong FY2028 revenue growth that eased investor fears about an AI capex slowdown. The report validated the ongoing AI infrastructure supercycle and drove Nasdaq futures +0.66% into Thursday's pre-open.

deals.headline: Lakers $12.5B Sale: Bob Iger & Joshua Kushner Buy NBA Premier Franchise
deals.description: Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner completed a record $12.5 billion acquisition of the Los Angeles Lakers from the Buss family, the largest sports franchise sale in history. The deal underscores the sustained premium that institutional capital is placing on live sports content rights.
deals.impact: Medium — signals continued sports media M&A wave

deals.headline: AI Enterprise Earnings Beat Trilogy: Salesforce, CrowdStrike, Okta
deals.description: Salesforce, CrowdStrike, and Okta all reported strong Q2 results, citing AI-driven expansion deals and accelerating customer net revenue retention as enterprise AI adoption enters a new phase. S&P 500 Q2 EPS growth is now tracking +50% YoY.
deals.impact: High — validates enterprise software AI monetization thesis

deals.headline: Alibaba Divests Video Game Unit for $1.5B+ as China Restructuring Continues
deals.description: Alibaba agreed to sell its video game business for at least $1.5 billion as part of its ongoing corporate restructuring and refocus on core e-commerce and cloud operations. The divestiture is the latest in a series of non-core asset sales as Alibaba streamlines under regulatory and competitive pressure.
deals.impact: Medium — Alibaba balance sheet improvement, signals China tech restructuring ongoing

runs.market_commentary:
Asian equities were broadly constructive overnight, with the Nikkei 225 adding roughly +0.5% as yen softness and sustained AI-sector enthusiasm supported risk appetite. Bloomberg's Asia wrap headlined 'Asian stocks set to gain as oil extends declines,' with Brent crude sliding on demand concerns and a firmer dollar. Australian July CPI was the key regional data point, watched closely for any signs of re-acceleration that could complicate the RBA's easing trajectory. Hang Seng and broader EM indices traded mixed as Chinese macro sentiment remained cautious.

European markets closed with modest gains: the DAX rose +0.61% to 26,266 and the FTSE 100 advanced +0.29% to 10,886. Energy and utilities were mild drags given crude's continued slide, while industrial and tech names contributed positively. Volumes were light with no major European macro surprises, as traders awaited the heavy US data and event slate.

US equity futures are trading cautiously lower pre-market: S&P 500 futures off ~0.04%, Dow futures barely green at +0.06%, and Nasdaq-100 futures lagging at -0.39% — software names are the primary drag. Two binary catalysts dominate the tape: July PCE inflation at 8:30 AM ET and Nvidia's FQ2 FY2027 earnings after the close (consensus $2.09 EPS, $92.2B revenue, +97.4% YoY). Consumer Confidence came in at 89.4 in August, a miss vs. the 90.2 consensus, adding a modest headwind.

ideas.catalyst: FQ2 FY2027 earnings report due after close today; consensus EPS $2.09 (~+100% YoY), revenue $92.2B (+97.4% YoY).
ideas.thesis: Nvidia's Blackwell architecture is ramping into record hyperscaler capex cycles; a revenue or gross-margin beat plus upbeat data-center guidance could drive a meaningful gap-up. Underlying demand from AWS, Azure, Google, and Meta for GB200 clusters remains structurally robust and supply-constrained.
ideas.key_risk: Beat-and-retreat dynamic if guidance only meets elevated consensus; any softer data-center color would disappoint.

ideas.catalyst: UBS upgraded to Buy from Neutral today, raising price target to $1,400 from $960, implying ~46% upside.
ideas.thesis: argenx's Vyvgart platform is expanding across multiple autoimmune indications; UBS sees meaningful revenue upside not priced in. The company's differentiated mechanism of action and growing global commercial footprint underpin a durable competitive position.
ideas.key_risk: Any clinical setback in pipeline programs could sharply reverse the sentiment-driven upgrade.

ideas.catalyst: FDA PDUFA decision due August 27 on once-daily HIV regimen; Trodelvy EU approval already secured; Q2 revenue +10% to $7.8B.
ideas.thesis: The pending FDA decision on a once-daily single-tablet HIV regimen could materially expand Gilead's dominant HIV franchise. Trodelvy's EU win and robust HIV sales trajectory support fundamental upside.
ideas.key_risk: FDA rejection or complete response letter would materially pressure shares.

ideas.catalyst: Positive clinical trial data released today; shares +8.5% in pre-market trading.
ideas.thesis: A meaningful positive clinical readout validates Summit's pipeline and frequently attracts partnership or M&A interest. Early-stage catalysts of this magnitude tend to sustain multi-session momentum as analyst initiations follow.
ideas.key_risk: Small-cap binary risk remains; subsequent data sets may fail to replicate initial positive signal.

ideas.catalyst: Q2 EPS and revenue beat with raised full-year sales forecast; shares +11.5% pre-market.
ideas.thesis: Abercrombie's brand transformation continues to outperform even in a softening consumer backdrop; management's raised FY guidance signals genuine confidence in H2 execution. The outsized pre-market move on elevated volume typically draws momentum-driven follow-through.
ideas.key_risk: Consumer spending deceleration more severe than anticipated could compress margins and force a FY guidance reversal.

ideas.catalyst: UBS upgraded to Buy from Neutral; price target raised to $42 from $36.
ideas.thesis: SolarEdge has been severely de-rated after a prolonged downcycle; UBS's upgrade signals a potential bottoming process as European residential solar demand recovers. Risk/reward is asymmetric at historically depressed valuations.
ideas.key_risk: Further deterioration in European residential solar demand or continued pricing pressure from Chinese competitors.

ideas.catalyst: Q3 guidance miss drives -6.2% pre-market despite Q2 earnings beat.
ideas.thesis: Zoom is caught in a structural squeeze as Microsoft Teams and Google Meet erode enterprise market share, limiting pricing power. The guidance miss confirms ongoing growth deceleration likely to persist into FY2027.
ideas.key_risk: Strategic M&A interest from a larger platform player could create a short-squeeze premium.

ideas.catalyst: Shares -9.2% pre-market after weak FY guidance overshadows Q2 EPS beat.
ideas.thesis: Intuit's weak FY guidance signals softening SMB spending and emerging competitive pressure from AI-native alternatives. Guidance resets at premium multiples are disproportionately punishing.
ideas.key_risk: Guidance could prove conservative; AI-powered products could accelerate user growth beyond current assumptions.

ideas.catalyst: Disappointing Q2 net sales and comparable sales; shares -7.4% pre-market.
ideas.thesis: Kohl's faces sustained structural headwinds from the shift to off-price retail and e-commerce. The Q2 comp sales miss confirms its brand repositioning is failing to gain traction.
ideas.key_risk: Activist investor accumulation or LBO speculation could generate a short-squeeze dynamic.

ideas.theme: Natural Gas Infrastructure — Data Center Demand
ideas.catalyst: Wolfe Research upgraded to Outperform from Peer Perform today with a $145 price target.
ideas.thesis: Natural gas demand growth driven by data center power needs and LNG export volumes makes midstream infrastructure a secular beneficiary. DT Midstream's pure-play natural gas exposure gives direct leverage to this structural tailwind.
ideas.key_risk: Natural gas price weakness or regulatory setbacks on pipeline permitting could delay volume growth.
